rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letters introduce signs of the Book whose contents are clear.
rows.anchor: الر تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means “so that”; revelation in Arabic lets its hearers understand, whereas a non-Arabic Qur'an would not be understood by them.
rows.anchor: ما فيه لو كان القرآن غير عربي ما فهموه ولا عقلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Best stories” means the Qur'an; the revelation phrase means what God revealed, paralleling 36:27, and the Prophet had been unaware of it before the Qur'an descended.
rows.anchor: أحسن القصص } ، يعني القرآن، { بمآ أوحينآ إليك } ، بالذي أوحينا إليك، نظيرها في يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Joseph's dream the eleven stars, sun, and moon descended from heaven to earth before prostrating to him.
rows.anchor: في المنام { أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر } هبطوا إلى الأرض من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eleven stars are Joseph's brothers; the sun is his mother Rachel, daughter of Latan, Jacob's maternal uncle.
rows.anchor: فالكواكب الأحد عشر إخوته، والشمس أم يوسف، وهي راحيل بنت لاتان، ولاتان هو خال يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon is his father Jacob, son of Isaac and Abraham, and Joseph already knew the dream's interpretation.
rows.anchor: والقمر أبوه يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم، وقد علم تعبير ما رأى يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob implies that the brothers would envy Joseph; “plot” means doing him harm, and Satan is an evident enemy to people.
rows.anchor: فيحسدوك إضمار، { فيكيدوا لك كيدا } ، فيعملوا بك شرا، { إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says God will select Joseph through their prostration and teach him dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: يقول: وهكذا يستخلصك ربك بالسجود، { ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث } ، يعني ويعلمك تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “House of Jacob” here comprises Joseph, his wife, and his eleven brothers; God's completed blessing on them is their prostration to Joseph.
rows.anchor: يعني بآل يعقوب هو وامرأته وإخوته الأحد عشر، بالسجود لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completed the blessing on Abraham and Isaac: Abraham was saved from fire and from sacrificing his son, and Isaac appears in Abraham's dream of sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وألقى إبراهيم في النار، فنجاه الله تعالى منها، وأراد ذبح ابنه، فخلصه الله بالسجود، { وإسحاق } في رؤيا إبراهيم في ذبح إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the blessing's completion; “wise” means the one who ordains it.
rows.anchor: { إن ربك عليم } بتمامها، { حكيم } [آية: 6]، يعني القاضي لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs for questioners were that Jews asked the Prophet about Joseph and his story became a sign for those questioners.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن اليهود لما سمعوا ذكر يوسف، عليه السلام، من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the Jews who heard the Prophet's account were Ka'b al-Ashraf, Huyayy and Jaddi ibn Akhtab, al-Nu'man ibn Awfa, Amr, Buhayra, Ghazal, and Malik ibn al-Dayf.
rows.anchor: منهم كعب بن الأشرف، وحيي، وجدي ابنا أخطب، والنعمان بن أوفى، وعمرو، وبحيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of those named Jews, only Jabr, Yasar Abu Fukayha, and Addas believed in the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فلم يؤمن بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم غير جبر غلام بن الحضرمي، ويسار أبو فكيهه، وعداس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's beauty surpassed people of his time like the full moon among the other stars.
rows.anchor: وكان يوسف قد فضل في زمانه بحسنه على الناس كفضل القمر ليلة البدر على سائر الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reuben was the oldest brother by age; Judah was greatest in judgment and is the “eldest” in 12:80 in that sense.
rows.anchor: وهو: روبيل أكبرهم سنا، ويهوذا أكبرهم في العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “band” means ten brothers; their claim that Jacob was plainly astray means obvious loss and distress from his love and mention of Joseph.
rows.anchor: ونحن عصبة } ، يعني عشرة، { إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين } [آية: 8]، يعني خسران مبين، يعني في شقاء بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers listed are Simon, Levi, Naphtali, Zebulun, Asher, Issachar, Gad, Dan, Joseph, and Benjamin, besides Reuben and Judah.
rows.anchor: وشمعون, ولاوى، ونفتولن، وربولن، وآشر، واستاخر، وجاب ودان، ويوسف وبنيامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They propose killing Joseph or casting him into a distant land so their father's attention turns to them.
rows.anchor: يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا } بعيدة، { يخل لكم وجه أبيكم } فيقبل عليكم بوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to become righteous afterward means that their affairs and standing with their father would be repaired.
rows.anchor: يعني وتصيروا { من بعده قوما صالحين } [آية: 9]، يعني يصلح أمركم وحالكم عند أبيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker is Judah son of Jacob; he opposes killing Joseph as a grave act and proposes leaving him in an unseen well by the travelers' route.
rows.anchor: وهو يهوذا بن يعقوب: { لا تقتلوا يوسف } فإن قتله عظيم، { و } لكن { وألقوه في غيابة الجب } على طريق الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well's “hidden place” is the portion concealed from sight; travelers would find Joseph and take him away, relieving the brothers of him.
rows.anchor: يعني الزائغة من البئر ما يتوارى عن العين ولا يراه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers claim they are sincere advisers to their father about Joseph.
rows.anchor: قالوا يأبانا ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف وإنا له لناصحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Let him graze and play” means let him be active and happy; Arabs use “I frolicked for you” to mean “I rejoiced for you.”
rows.anchor: يعني ينشط ويفرح، والعرب تقول: رتعت لك، يعني فرحت لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers promise to protect Joseph from being lost.
rows.anchor: وإنا له لحافظون } [آية: 12] من الضيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob fears that a wolf will eat Joseph while the brothers are inattentive; the land had many wolves, explaining this fear.
rows.anchor: لا تشعرون به، وكانت أرضا مذئبة، فمن ثم قال يعقوب: أنى أخاف أن يأكله الذئب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten brothers mean that if a wolf ate Joseph while they were a group, they would be helpless failures.
rows.anchor: أي العشرة،: { لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة } ، يعني ونحن جماعة، { إنآ إذا لخاسرون } [آية: 14]، يعني لعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers threw Joseph into a well three parasangs away, whose water was dark and thick but became clear and fresh when he entered it.
rows.anchor: على رأس ثلاثة فراسخ، فألقوه في الجب، والماء يومئذ كدر غليظ، فعذب الماء وصفا حين ألقى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph stood on a rock at the well's far side; God assigned an angel to guard and feed him there.
rows.anchor: وقام على صخرة في قاصية البئر، فوكل الله به ملكا يحرسه في الجب ويطعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Joseph that he would later tell his brothers what they had done while they did not realize he was Joseph; he later exposed their cruelty through the cup.
rows.anchor: عليه السلام، بعدما انصرف إخوته: إنك ستخبر إخوتك بأمرهم هذا الذي ركبوا منك، ثم قال: { وهم لا يشعرون } أنك يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Joseph later struck the vessel, he told his brothers that it disclosed their evil treatment and stripping his clothes.
rows.anchor: فأنبأهم يوسف بعد ذلك حين قال لهم وضرب الإناء، فقال: إن الإناء ليخبرني بما فعلتم بيوسف من الشر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains that the brothers did not realize the speaker was Joseph.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل في قوله: { وأوحينآ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph secretly instructed his trustee to strike the cup three times and pretend its tone revealed that the brothers were children of one mother who had become divided and hostile.
rows.anchor: فقال له: أحضر الصاع إذا حضروا وانقره ثلاث نقرات، واستمع طنين كل نقرة حتى تسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cup's first supposed disclosure was that the brothers had told Joseph they shared one mother but were divided, which explained their strife.
rows.anchor: فقال: أيها الملك، إن الصاع يقول لك: إنهم أخبروك أنهم لأم واحدة، وأنهم شتى، وذلك وقع بينهم ما يقع بين الأولاد العتاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cup's second tap disclosed a missing brother whose arrival would reveal the brothers' story.
rows.anchor: ثم نقره الثانية وأصغى إليه يسمعه، فلما سكن، قال: أيها الملك، إنهم أخبروك أن لهم أخا مفقودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third tap says the brothers caused their father's every grief.
rows.anchor: إنه ما دخل على أبيهم غم ولا هم ولا حزن إلا بسببهم وجرائرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers feared exposure, approached Joseph together, and begged him by his prophetic qualities to overlook their offense.
rows.anchor: وخافوا أن يظهر عليهم ما كتموه من أمر يوسف، عليه السلام، فقاموا إليه بجمعهم يقبلون رأسه وعينه، ويقولون: بالذي أشبهك بالنبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph relented, saying he would have punished them as thieves had he not respected their father, and ordered them to leave.
rows.anchor: فرق لهم، وقال: لولا حفاظي لكم في أبيكم لنكلت بكم ولألحقتكم بالسراق واللصوص، أغربوا عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers told Jacob what happened; he returned the merchandise and sent a letter identifying his lineage through Isaac and Abraham.
rows.anchor: فردهم بالبضاعة المجازة، وكتب معهم كتابا إليه، فيه: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، من يعقوب إسرائيل الله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's letter says his family is tested: Abraham survived fire, Isaac was spared sacrifice, and Jacob suffered the loss of beloved Joseph.
rows.anchor: ما سرقت، ولا ولدت سارقا، ولكن أهل بيت البلاء موكل بنا، أما جدي، فألقي في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king wept while reading Jacob's letter and inferred that its sender was the father; Joseph then identified himself and his brothers recognized him.
rows.anchor: فلما قرأ كتابه انتحب، فقيل له: كأنك صاحب الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan was an Arab party traveling toward Egypt; two men, Malik ibn D'ar and Awad ibn Amir, were sent to fetch water, and Malik lowered the bucket.
rows.anchor: وهي العير، وقالوا: رفقة من العرب، فنزلوا على البئر يريدون مصر، { فأرسلوا واردهم } ، فبعثوا رجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph caught the bucket; Malik called to Awad with good news that a boy was there, and the well lay in Jordan's valley at Adnan.
rows.anchor: فتعلق يوسف بالدلو، فصاح مالك { قال } ، فقال: يا عود، للذي يسقي، وهو عود بن عامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph and even the well, trees, stones, and earth wept; the brothers had stripped and tied him, mocked his request for a shirt by invoking his dream, then threw him down, but God saved him.
rows.anchor: فبكى يوسف، عليه السلام، وبكى الجب لبكائه، وبكى مد صوته من الشجر والمدر والحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph prayed that God grant Malik a child; Malik subsequently had twenty-four sons.
rows.anchor: ودعا يوسف ربه حين أخرجه مالك أن يهب لمالك ولدا، فولد له أربعة وعشرون ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The finders concealed Joseph from their caravan companions and falsely called him merchandise for the water-drawers so others would not claim a share.
rows.anchor: يعني أخفوه من أصحابهم الذين مروا على الماء في الرفقة، وقالوا: هو بضاعة لأهل الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their lying claim about Joseph being merchandise.
rows.anchor: يعني بما يقولون من الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They sold him” means they sold a free person unlawfully, since both the price of a free person and his sale are forbidden.
rows.anchor: يعني وباعوه { بثمن بخس } بثمن حرام لا يحل لهم بيعة؛ لأنه حر، وثمن الحر حرام وبيعه حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counted dirhams were twenty; Arabs called amounts below forty counted dirhams, while forty made an uqiyya.
rows.anchor: عشرون درهما، وكانت العرب تبايع بالأقل، فإذا كانت أربعين فهي أوقية، وما كان دون الأربعين، فهي دراهم معدودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sellers were indifferent to Joseph because they did not know his standing with God or his parentage; had they known, they would not have sold him.
rows.anchor: ولم يعلموا منزلة يوسف عند الله، ومن أبوه، ولو علموا ذلك ما باعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Near Egypt Joseph asked rider Malik ibn D'ar al-Lakhmi, headed to Canaan, to greet Jacob and describe him; Jacob prayed for the rider's childless wife, who then bore twenty-four sons.
rows.anchor: فبينا هو قريب منها، إذ مر براكب منها يقال له: مالك بن دعر اللخمي، قال له يوسف: أين تريد أيها الراكب؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchaser sold Joseph to Qitfir ibn Misha for twenty dinars, an extra garment, and two sandals; the seller received the dinars' value in dirhams.
rows.anchor: فاشتراه قطفير بن ميشا بعشرين دينارا وزيادة حلة ونعلين، { وأخذ البائع قيمة الدنانير دراهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian purchaser is Qitfir ibn Misha and his wife Zulaikha daughter of Yamlika; he asks her to give Joseph good lodging and care.
rows.anchor: وهو قطفير بن ميشا { لامرأته } زليخا بنت يمليخا: { أكرمي مثواه } ، يعني أحسني منزلته وولايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitfir hopes Joseph will benefit them or that they may adopt him as a son.
rows.anchor: عسى أن ينفعنا } أو نصيب منه خيرا، { أو نتخذه ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God empowered Joseph with kingship and authority in Egypt and would teach him dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض } الملك والسلطان في أرض مصر، { ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث } ، يعني من تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings Joseph's destined outcome to completion despite what people know; most people do not know this.
rows.anchor: يعني والله متم ليوسف أمره الذي هو كائن مما لا يعلمه الناس، فذلك قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph reached full strength at eighteen; “judgment” means understanding, and God rewards sincere doers with understanding and knowledge.
rows.anchor: يعني ثماني عشرة سنة، { آتيناه حكما } ، يقول: أعطيناه فهما، { وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman shut the doors on herself and Joseph for intercourse; “come to me” means she offered herself and pressed him with words.
rows.anchor: على نفسها وعلى يوسف في أمر الجماع، { وقالت هيت لك } ، يعني هلم لك نفسي، تريد المرأة الجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph sought God's protection; “my lord” means his master, the woman's husband, who had treated him well, and wronging the master's household would not prosper.
rows.anchor: يقول: إنه سيدي، يعني زوجها، أكرم مثواي، يعني منزلتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that Joseph experienced desire for her as strong as that of forty men.
rows.anchor: وألقى عليها شهوة أربعين إنسانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman lay down for intercourse; Joseph loosened his trousers and sat between her legs, but would have proceeded only if he had not seen his Lord's sign.
rows.anchor: يقول: همت المرأة بيوسف حتى استلقت للجماع، { وهم بها } يوسف حين حل سراويله وجلس بين رجليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign appeared as Jacob biting his finger; Joseph turned away and the woman followed him.
rows.anchor: والبرهان مثل له يعثوب عاض على إصبعه، فلما رأى ذلك، ولى دبرا واتبعته المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Evil” means sin and “indecency” means sins; Joseph was among God's chosen servants through prophethood and messengerhood, as in 38:46.
rows.anchor: يعني هكذا، { لنصرف عنه السوء } ، يعني الإثم، { والفحشآء } ، يعني المعاصي، { إنه من عبادنا المخلصين } [آية: 24] بالنبوة والرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph fled ahead and the woman pursued him to detain him; she caught him near the door and tore his shirt from behind until it fell off.
rows.anchor: يوسف أمامها هارب منها، وهي ورائه تتبعه لتحبسه على نفسها، فأدركته قبل أن ينتهي إلى الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They found” means “they encountered,” as in 2:170; her master is her husband, and her cousin Yamlakha son of Azlikha was also at the door.
rows.anchor: يعني عند الباب ومعه ابن عمها يملخا بن أزليخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman accuses Joseph of seeking adultery and demands prison or painful beating.
rows.anchor: يعني الزنا، { إلا أن يسجن } حبسا في نصب، { أو عذاب أليم } [آية: 25]، يعني ضربا وجيعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness was the woman's cousin Yamlakha ibn her uncle; he proposes that a tear at the front would support her accusation and make Joseph a liar.
rows.anchor: وهو يمليخا ابن عم المرأة، فتكلم بعقل ولب، قال: { إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Joseph had pursued her, she would have torn the front of his shirt, making her truthful and Joseph's denial false.
rows.anchor: أي إن كان يوسف هو الذي راودها، فقدت، يعني فمزقت قميصه من قبل، يعني من قدامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tear from behind means Joseph fled from her, so the woman lied and Joseph spoke truthfully.
rows.anchor: أي وإن كان يوسف هو الهارب منها، فأدركته فقدت قميصه من دبر، فكذبت على يوسف، ويوسف من الصادقين في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They heard the pair's commotion and the shirt tearing behind the door.
rows.anchor: وقد سمعا جلبتهما وتمزيق القميص من وراء الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband says the torn shirt is their plotting and calls women's plotting great because a woman keeps pursuing a man until he commits a grave sin.
rows.anchor: يقول: مزق من ورائه، { قال } لها: { إنه من كيدكن } ، يقول: تمزيق القميص من فعلكن، يعني امرأته، ثم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness tells Joseph to forget the incident and tell no one, then tells the woman to apologize to her husband and ask him not to punish her.
rows.anchor: الأمر الذي فعلت بك، ولا تذكره لأحد، ثم أقبل الشاهد على المرأة، فقال: { واستغفري لذنبك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman is counted among those who erred.
rows.anchor: إنك كنت من الخاطئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gossips were five wives: of the baker, cupbearer, prison keeper, animal keeper, and chamberlain; they say the Aziz's Canaanite slave is pursued by his wife, consumed by love and in evident distress.
rows.anchor: وهن خمس نسوة: امرأة الخباز، وامرأة الساقي وامرأة صاحب السجن، وامرأة صاحب الدواب، وامرأة صاحب الإذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Her love pierced her heart” means love overwhelmed her intensely, and “manifest error” means clear loss and distress from loving Joseph.
rows.anchor: يعني غلبها حبا شديدا هلكت عليه، { إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين } [آية: 30]، يعني في خسران بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zulaikha interpreted their “plotting” as their remarks, invited them, and prepared citron; any food cut with a knife is called a muttaka.
rows.anchor: يعني بقولهن لها، { أرسلت إليهن } فجئنها، { وأعتدت لهن متكئا } ، وهو الأترج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She gave each woman a knife, had Joseph dress and groom himself, and says his beauty was one-third, inherited through Isaac, Sarah, Eve, and Adam.
rows.anchor: وأمرت يوسف، عليه السلام، فتزين وترجل، وكان أعطى يوسف في زمانه ثلث الحسن، وآتاه الحسن من قبل جده إسحاق

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says males are more beautiful than females among all things, and Joseph's beauty surpassed people of his age like the full moon among stars.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كل ذكر أحسن من الأنثى من الأشياء كلها، وفضل يوسف في زمانه بحسنه على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the messenger reported the women's words, Joseph says he wants his master to know he did not betray him in his absence or violate his household.
rows.anchor: يقول: هذا ليعلم سيده { أني لم أخنه بالغيب } في أهله، ولم أخالفه فيهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide or set right adulterers' plots; he abandons them and does not protect them from adultery.
rows.anchor: يعني لا يصلح عمل الزناة، يقول: يخذلهم، فلا يعصمهم من الزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king, identified here as Gabriel, came with the proof Joseph had seen and asked where his earlier intention had been when he loosened his trousers and sat between her legs.
rows.anchor: فأتاه الملك، وهو جبريل، بالبرهان الذي رأى، فقال ليوسف: أين ما هممت به أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph does not declare his heart innocent: he had desired her; the self means the heart and urges the body toward sin, except where God protects it.
rows.anchor: يعني قلبي من الهم، لقد هممت بها، { إن النفس } ، يعني القلب { لأمارة بالسوء } للجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives Joseph for the contemplated sin and shows mercy by protecting him.
rows.anchor: لما هم به من المعصية، { رحيم } [آية: 53] به حين عصمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king wants to take Joseph as his own; after speaking with him, the king calls him high-ranking and trustworthy over what is entrusted to him.
rows.anchor: يعني أتخذه، { فلما } أتاه يوسف و { كلمه } ، أي كلم الملك، { قال } ليوسف:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Established” means esteemed among the king's people; the phrase is paralleled by 81:20.
rows.anchor: يقول: عندنا وجيه، { أمين } [آية: 54] على ما وكلت به، كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to oversee Egypt's storehouses, describing himself as reliable with his duties and knowledgeable of every people's language.
rows.anchor: بمصر، { إني حفيظ } لما وكلتني به، { عليم } [آية: 55]، يعني عالم بلغة الناس كلها.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil reports the Prophet saying Joseph would have ruled that very day had he added “God willing” to his claim of reliability and knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لو قال: إني حفيظ عليم إن شاء الله، لملك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph waited another year and a half before ruling Egypt.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لبث بعد ذلك سنة ونصفا، ثم ملك أرض مصر.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil reports the Prophet marveling at Joseph's patience and generosity and saying he himself would have hurried to the door when summoned.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " عجبت من صبر يوسف وكرمه، والله يغفر له، لو كنت أنا لبادرت الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God empowered Joseph with kingship in Egypt; “settle” means reside wherever he wished, and “mercy” means God's bounty, with reward fully repaid.
rows.anchor: يعني وهكذا مكنا ليوسف الملك { في الأرض } ، في أرض مصر، ل { يتبوأ } ، يقول: ينزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewarded Joseph's patience through affliction and resistance to sin by making him ruler of Egypt.
rows.anchor: فجزاه الله بالصبر على البلاء، والصبر على المعصية بأن ملكه على مصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife reward is greater than worldly kingship for those who affirm divine oneness and avoid associating partners, as Joseph did.
rows.anchor: يعني أكبر، يعني جزاء الآخرة أفضل مما أعطي في الدنيا من الملك، { للذين آمنوا } ، يعني صدقوا بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers came from Canaan; Joseph recognized them, but they did not know him and said they were Jacob's sons from Canaan.
rows.anchor: من أرض كنعان، { فدخلوا عليه } ، أي على يوسف بمصر، { فعرفهم } يوسف، { وهم له منكرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked why only ten brothers came, they said one brother remained with their father after his brother was eaten by a wolf, so he could rest.
rows.anchor: قالوا: نحن أحد عشر، قال: ما لي لا أرى الأحد عشر؟ قالوا: واحد منا عند أبينا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks for Benjamin, their brother by their father and Joseph's full brother, promising a full measure and saying he is Egypt's best host.
rows.anchor: يعني بنيامين، وكان أخاهم من أبيهم، وكان أخا يوسف لأبيه وأمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without Benjamin, they will get no food sale from Joseph and may not approach his land.
rows.anchor: يعني فلا بيع لكم { عندي } من الطعام، { ولا تقربون } [آية: 60] بلادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers promise to try to persuade Jacob about Benjamin and say they will do it.
rows.anchor: يعقوب، { وإنا لفاعلون } [آية: 61] ذلك بأبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's young servants measure the food; he orders them to return the brothers' dirhams in their bags so they notice and come back, since lack of money should not detain them and they are herders.
rows.anchor: يعني لخدامه وهم يكيلون لهم الطعام، { اجعلوا بضاعتهم } ، يعني دراهمهم { في رحالهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they return, the brothers say food measure was withheld and ask Jacob to send Benjamin so they can obtain their measure.
rows.anchor: يعني منع كيل الطعام، فيه إضمار فيما يستأنف، { فأرسل معنا أخانا } بنيامين { نكتل } الطعام بثمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers again promise to guard Benjamin from being lost.
rows.anchor: وإنا له لحافظون } [آية: 63] من الضيعة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: In Ibn Masud's reading, Jacob asks whether they will guard Benjamin as they guarded Joseph before.
rows.anchor: في قراءة ابن مسعود: هل تحفظونه إلا كما حفظتم أخاه يوسف من قبل بنيامين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is a better protector than the brothers, and “most merciful” means the best of those who show mercy.
rows.anchor: يعني فالله خير حافظا منكم، { وهو أرحم الراحمين } [آية: 64]، يعني أفضل الراحمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening their baggage means opening their containers; they find their dirhams returned and ask what more they could want.
rows.anchor: يعني حلوا أوعيتهم، { وجدوا بضاعتهم } ، يعني دراهمهم، فيها إضمار، { ردت إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they will bring food for their family, protect Benjamin, and gain an additional camel-load because of him.
rows.anchor: هذه { بضاعتنا } ، يعني دراهمنا { ردت إلينا ونمير أهلنا } الطعام، { ونحفظ أخانا } بنيامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egypt sold food by the number of people rather than animals because food was scarce; the extra measure was quick and unheld.
rows.anchor: وكان أهل مصر يبيعون الطعام على عدة الرجال، ولا يبيعون على عدة الدواب، وكان الطعام عزيزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob demands God's solemn pledge that they bring Benjamin back and not lose him as they lost Joseph, except if all are overcome by death.
rows.anchor: يعني تعطوني عهدا من الله، { لتأتنني به } ، يعني بنيامين ولا تضيعوه كما ضيعتم أخاه يوسف، { إلا أن يحاط بكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob calls God witness between them, as in 28:28.
rows.anchor: يعني شهيدا بيني وبينكم، نظيرها في القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob fears the evil eye because his sons are handsome and tells them to enter Egypt by separate routes and gates.
rows.anchor: فلما سرح بنيامين معهم، خشي عليهم العين، وكان بنوه لهم جمال وحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their precautions cannot avert God's decree; judgment belongs to God, in whom Jacob trusts, and the trusting should trust Him.
rows.anchor: يعني ما القضاء إلا لله، { عليه توكلت } ، يقول: به أثق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “On Him let the trusting rely” means the trusting should place their confidence in Him.
rows.anchor: وعليه فليتوكل المتوكلون } [آية: 67]، يعني به فليثق الواثقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers each entered by a separate road; this could not avert God's decree, only satisfy a concern in Jacob's heart, in an Arabic idiom also found at 59:9.
rows.anchor: أخذ كل واحد منهم في طريق على حدة، يقول الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob has knowledge because God taught him that his sons would suffer only what God decreed; most people do not know this.
rows.anchor: يعني أباهم { لذو علم لما علمناه }؛ لأن الله تعالى علمه أنه لا يصيب بنيه إلا ما قضى الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph took Benjamin close and privately told him he was his brother, so he should not grieve over the brothers' actions.
rows.anchor: يعني ضم إليه أخاه، { قال إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يعملون } [آية: 69]،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's reassurance refers to the brothers taking the returned dirhams from their baggage and bringing them back to him.
rows.anchor: يقول: فلا تحزن بما سرقوك وجاءوا بالدراهم التي كانت في أوعيتهم فردوها إلى يوسف، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After provisioning them, Joseph puts in Benjamin's bag the drinking vessel used by the king.
rows.anchor: وهى الإناء الذى يشرب به الملك، { في رحل أخيه } بنيامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's attendant Ba'raim ibn Barbari, the caller, announces to the caravan that they are thieves; the brothers are dismayed and suspicious.
rows.anchor: يعني نادى مناد، اسمه بعرايم بن بربري، من فتيان يوسف: { أيتها العير } ، يعني الرفقة، { إنكم لسارقون } [آية: 70]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording places the brothers' turning toward the caller before their question about what was missing.
rows.anchor: فيها تقديم وأقبلوا على المنادي، ثم قالوا: { ماذا تفقدون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missing king's cup was a measuring vessel like those used by military people; its finder would earn a camel-load, and the announcer guarantees it.
rows.anchor: يعني إناء الملك، وكان يكال به كفعل أهل العساكر، { ولمن جاء به حمل بعير } ، يعني وقر بعير، { وأنا به زعيم } [آية: 72]، يعني به كفيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers deny coming to corrupt Egypt with sins and say returned money proves they were not thieves.
rows.anchor: فرد الإخوة القول على المنادى، { قالوا تالله لقد علمتم ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض } ، يعني أرض مصر بالمعاصي، { وما كنا سارقين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller and companions ask what punishment the brothers propose if they are lying.
rows.anchor: قالوا } ، أي المنادي ومن معه: { فما جزآؤه } ، أي السارق، { إن كنتم كاذبين } [آية: 74]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say the person found with the cup in his baggage is the punishment for the theft; this is how thieves are punished, paralleling 5:39.
rows.anchor: من تاب من بعد ظلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptian law made a thief compensate with a servant employed at twice the stolen amount and then released; Canaanite law made the thief serve for the stolen amount, then go free.
rows.anchor: وكان الحكم بأرض مصر أن يغرم السارق عبدا يستخدم على قدر ضعف ما سرق ويترك، وكان الحكم بأرض كنعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers applied Canaan's law while in Egypt.
rows.anchor: ثم يخلى سبيله، فيذهب حيث شاء، فحكموا بأرض مصر بقضاء أرضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller searched the brothers' bags first; when he found nothing, they insisted he inspect Benjamin's bag, where the vessel was found.
rows.anchor: فبدأ } المنادي { بأوعيتهم } ، فنظر فيها، فلم ير شيئا، { قبل وعاء أخيه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's plan let Joseph keep Benjamin as a servant under the king's law; normally the king's law only required double compensation, unless God willed otherwise.
rows.anchor: { كذلك كدنا } ، يعني هكذا صنعنا { ليوسف } أن يأخذ أخاه خادما بسرقته في دين الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised Joseph's standing for taking his brother; God is above every knower, and Joseph knew more than his brothers.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: { وفوق كل ذي علم عليم } [آية: 76]، يقول الرب تعالى عالم، { وفوق كل ذي علم عليم } ، يقول: يوسف أعلم إخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers claim Benjamin's brother Joseph had stolen earlier; their story was that Joseph took a golden idol from his maternal grandfather Latan at Rachel's request to stop his idolatry.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن جد يوسف أبا أمه كان اسمه لاتان، كان يعبد الأصنام، فقالت راحيل لابنها يوسف، عليه السلام: خذ الصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph kept their accusation inside and did not show it, thinking they were worse in conduct; God knew their false description of his theft.
rows.anchor: فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم } ، ولم يظهرها لهم، { قال } في نفسه: { أنتم شر مكانا }
